evals.prompt: Turn this repository's current data workflow into a user- and agent-friendly CLI. Users should be able to run the recommended ZIP-to-processed-dataset path and adjust paths, seed, archive assignments, split ratios, and preprocessing settings through a root-level TOML file or CLI overrides without editing Python. Expose the existing extraction, interim, validation, and dataset-builder scripts as discoverable commands, repair the installed console entry point if needed, add tests, and update both AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md with copy-pasteable commands and config precedence.
evals.expected_output: A working Typer CLI with an installed entry point, TOML configuration and explicit override precedence, commands for the existing workflows, tests, synchronized AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md documentation, and a verified temporary-fixture smoke run.
expectations: The installed console entry point and root --help expose the CLI plus data/config command groups.
A root-level TOML configuration and explicit CLI override precedence cover the requested dataset settings without source edits.
Existing dataset and script implementations are called directly rather than duplicated or shell-launched from the new CLI.
Both AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md document the same canonical commands, config path, and precedence.
Focused tests and a temporary-fixture smoke path demonstrate the CLI works end to end.

evals.prompt: Make the dataset builder configurable for repeated experiments without source edits. Keep the existing preprocessing implementation as the source of truth, add a checked-in tb-detection.toml example plus config init/show/validate commands, and support CLI overrides for the seed, input/output directories, target image size, split ratios, and logging level. Reject invalid cross-field values before processing, test precedence and errors, and document the exact commands in AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.
evals.expected_output: A typed configuration layer mapped to the existing dataset configuration, deterministic CLI/config precedence, preflight validation with actionable errors, focused tests, and synchronized documentation verified through the real CLI.
expectations: tb-detection.toml and config init/show/validate commands expose the requested dataset settings.
The implementation maps configuration into the existing typed dataset configuration rather than maintaining duplicate preprocessing constants.
The effective precedence is deterministic and CLI overrides take priority over config-file values.
Invalid split ratios, dimensions, or other cross-field values fail during validation before processing begins with an actionable error.
Tests cover precedence and invalid configuration, and both command documents describe the same contract.

evals.prompt: Add a safe command surface around all current data scripts in this Python repository. Include the recommended dataset command and clearly labeled legacy extract/interim commands, expose an incomplete validation script without pretending it works, and make every command discoverable through --help. Use the project's packaging conventions, avoid shelling out to source scripts, preserve raw data immutability, and report any unsupported command explicitly. Update the agent and contributor command references and run a smoke test with temporary input data.
evals.expected_output: A thin, package-installed CLI that routes to real implementations, clearly handles incomplete functionality, preserves existing behavior, updates both documentation files, and provides test/smoke evidence.
expectations: Help output exposes the recommended dataset command and clearly labeled extract, interim, and validation commands.
The incomplete validation path fails explicitly with an actionable unsupported/incomplete message instead of returning success.
The CLI calls real repository functions or gives a documented limitation; it does not shell out to source scripts or rewrite raw data.
AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md contain synchronized command references and identify the recommended versus legacy paths.
A temporary-input smoke run or focused test provides evidence for at least one real command and its exit behavior.
